status: Design proposal only. No loaded mod changes.

nodes.title: Contest Soviet Clients
nodes.description: American pressure needs a credible local partner and a political objective. African commitments extend this existing foreign-policy channel.
nodes.history: Existing US foreign-policy entry.
nodes.rp: The new regional sections branch from existing statecraft. The Kurdish campaigns and the China and Soviet channels keep their own programmes.

nodes.title: Regional Guarantees
nodes.description: Limited security commitments and negotiations can give regional governments alternatives to escalation.
nodes.history: Existing US foreign-policy entry.
nodes.rp: The diplomatic approach remains reachable through this existing channel.

nodes.title: The African Contest
nodes.description: Washington needs separate policies for liberation movements, established governments and negotiated settlements. A partner in one conflict may oppose American policy in another.
nodes.history: A regional expansion of the existing Kissinger branch.
nodes.rp: All four theatres remain visible. Governments can refuse terms, seek competing assistance or end a programme. Ordinary diplomacy stays available.

nodes.title: Authority and Oversight
nodes.description: The executive needs a lawful appropriation and a defensible account of the commitments it makes. Congressional restrictions can stop an armed programme even when a foreign partner wants it.
requirements: Congress can consider the proposed African appropriation.
effects: Unlock: Seek an African Assistance Appropriation
Unlock: Renew or Repeal an Angola Aid Restriction
nodes.history: Congressional opposition constrained the historical Angola operation.
nodes.rp: A real statutory aid ban suspends arms deliveries. A recorded political reversal is required to reopen them. Civilian talks and humanitarian assistance remain possible.

nodes.title: An African Understanding
nodes.description: The African competition can become part of a wider bargain with Moscow. Each government must specify which of its own missions it is prepared to end.
requirements: At least one African negotiating channel is active.
Linkage and Restraint has unlocked the existing regional cooperation programme.
The Soviet Union exists, is at peace with the USA and can receive the proposal.
effects: Cold War Tension: -1 point if the existing shared-relief limit and current tension permit

assets: Recall the selected American attaches and volunteers.
Deployed volunteer recall: -50 Political Power, -15 Command Power.
deals.term: While the signed joint programme is observed

assets: Recall the selected Soviet attaches and volunteers.
Deployed volunteer recall: -50 Political Power, -15 Command Power.
deals.term: While the signed joint programme is observed

nodes.history: Linkage with Moscow was part of American Angola policy.
nodes.rp: Uses the existing USA-Soviet treaty maker. Cuba controls its own forces and must agree separately. Neither Moscow nor Washington can sign for Angola or impose a local peace.

nodes.title: The Angolan Front
nodes.description: Angolan movements have their own leadership, constituencies and rivalries. Washington must establish political contact before deciding what to promise.
requirements: A relevant Angolan movement is politically active.
nodes.history: FNLA and UNITA were separate recipients of American support.
nodes.rp: Proposed rework of the existing focus: political contacts work before UNITA holds a country. Contact alone creates no state, army or civil war.

nodes.title: The FNLA Channel
nodes.description: Holden Roberto offers a northern political network and connections across the Congolese frontier. Its ambitions need not coincide with those of other Angolan movements.
requirements: FNLA retains an active local organisation.
nodes.history: FNLA had ties to Mobutu and received US aid.
nodes.rp: FNLA is a movement, not an invented state tag. A contact programme costs 0.00001% of US GDP per week while funded; the local host can disrupt its networks and transit.

nodes.title: The UNITA Channel
nodes.description: Jonas Savimbi represents a different organisation with its own regional base. A separate channel reduces dependence on a single claimant to Angolan power.
requirements: UNITA retains an active local organisation.
nodes.history: UNITA also received American support in 1975.
nodes.rp: The two contact channels may coexist. Funding reaches the organisation before a UNITA state exists. The proposed political programme costs 0.00001% of US GDP per week.

nodes.title: Back the Armed Opposition
nodes.description: Military assistance offers immediate leverage against a hostile armed rival, but ties American policy to the survival and conduct of the supported movement.
requirements: A civil conflict or documented armed threat exists.
An active appropriation permits military assistance.
An Angolan recipient force and an accepted supply route exist.

deals.term: While this assistance programme is active
While this assistance programme is active

nodes.history: Military assistance is based on the 1975 intervention.
nodes.rp: Exclusive active funding priority with the enhanced settlement programme. Basic contacts and ordinary mediation remain open. A later change of programme is allowed; it cannot repeat earlier deliveries.

nodes.title: Pursue an African Settlement
nodes.description: A coalition settlement could limit foreign intervention without requiring Washington to secure an outright battlefield victory for one claimant.
requirements: At least one Angolan movement accepts exploratory talks.
An African host accepts mediation.

deals.term: While this mediation programme is active
While this mediation programme is active

nodes.history: Alternative negotiated outcome, grounded in African mediation efforts.
nodes.rp: Competes with enhanced military funding, not with the existence of the opposition. A mediator may refuse or demand revised terms; no Angolan faction is forced into talks.

nodes.title: A Supervised Arms Pipeline
nodes.description: Reliable shipments, instructors and end-use inspection matter more than unbounded promises. The supply programme must remain accountable to its appropriation.
requirements: The partner force accepts end-use conditions.
The USA has 600 infantry weapons and 60 support equipment.
All transit governments have approved the route.
effects: Unlock: Request a Further Supervised Shipment
nodes.history: Material assistance and training were historical tools.
nodes.rp: A single paid shipment from actual American stockpiles. No free weekly equipment. A closed route, aid ban or refusal stops further consignments. No human transit country is bypassed.

nodes.title: An Angolan Round Table
nodes.description: A viable agreement needs the governing authority and the organisations still capable of fighting. External patrons can support the conference but cannot decide its outcome for them.
requirements: Angola and each participating armed organisation accept the negotiated settlement.
An agreed ceasefire is being observed.
nodes.history: Plausible alternative to a prolonged civil war.
nodes.rp: All affected parties approve the political settlement. The reconstruction grant goes only to the actual receiving government, including an agreed successor. An integrated movement does not receive a second state spirit or cash stream.

nodes.title: The Kinshasa Channel
nodes.description: Mobutu can offer regional connections and transit, but expects support for his own government. An American relationship with Zaire needs terms that survive disagreement.
requirements: Zaire exists and will receive a diplomatic proposal.
nodes.history: Zaire was a regional partner and an Angola transit route.
nodes.rp: Transit permission is a separate recipient choice. Signing political liaison does not place Zairean troops under American command.

nodes.title: Lusaka Consultations
nodes.description: Kenneth Kaunda has influence among neighbouring governments and liberation movements. Working with Zambia can widen American diplomacy beyond an exclusive dependence on Mobutu.
requirements: Zambia accepts a political consultation channel.
nodes.history: Kaunda was an important negotiating counterpart.
nodes.rp: Zambia can mediate without joining a US bloc. Political contact is compatible with Zambian positions on Angola, Rhodesia and South Africa.

nodes.title: Equip the Zairian Army
nodes.description: A better supplied national army can defend a vulnerable government, but assistance risks strengthening institutions that answer to Mobutu rather than the population.
requirements: Zaire requests assistance.
The American appropriation permits the programme.
The USA has 800 infantry weapons and 80 support equipment.
nodes.history: Security assistance is a historical approach; exact package is proposed.
nodes.rp: Competes with the enhanced reconstruction programme for the same Zaire aid appropriation. Basic diplomatic relations and crisis evacuation remain available.

nodes.title: Copperbelt Recovery
nodes.description: Restoring mining districts and commercial connections can give the government an alternative to permanent emergency funding. American investors seek predictable access rather than ownership by decree.
requirements: Zaire accepts the financing and investment terms.
nodes.history: Plausible economic alternative to a security-first commitment.
nodes.rp: The recipient setup charge uses Zairean GDP; the weekly grant uses US GDP. No invented copper or cobalt resource token. Actual investments still need their normal project approval.

nodes.title: The Shaba Air Bridge
nodes.description: Transport support can help an invited regional response and an evacuation effort during a real incursion into Shaba. Those missions have different objectives and commanders.
requirements: An actual Shaba/Katanga incursion or comparable armed crisis exists.
Zaire requests help.
France or Belgium separately accepts the transport arrangement.

deals.country: Each accepting French or Belgian mission

nodes.history: US aircraft supported distinct French and Belgian missions in 1978.
nodes.rp: An insurgent incursion can qualify without an interstate declaration of war. French protection, Belgian evacuation and other foreign troop deployments each require their own decisions.

nodes.title: Cross-Border Assurances
nodes.description: A border-security agreement can exchange an end to hostile sponsorship for trade and reconstruction. Verification depends on the obligations each government actually accepts.
requirements: Zaire and Angola accept reciprocal limits on their own support.
The named intermediary accepts the final paper.
nodes.history: Alternative bilateral settlement of regional sponsorship disputes.
nodes.rp: No automatic expulsion of refugees or destruction of local movements. Benefits suspend if a signatory resumes the specifically prohibited support.

nodes.title: The Ethiopian Partnership
nodes.description: Ethiopia already has a substantial American military relationship. Preserving useful cooperation requires listening to its own security concerns rather than treating it as an empty space on a strategic map.
requirements: Ethiopia is willing to continue or negotiate American cooperation.
nodes.history: Available from the 1970 setting: the partnership predates the Derg.
nodes.rp: Revolution or a change of alignment can terminate cooperation. Neither an Ethiopian revolution nor a Soviet alliance is triggered by this focus.

nodes.title: A Channel to Mogadishu
nodes.description: Dialogue can test whether Somalia wants room for manoeuvre. It need not wait for a complete break with its present supplier, but material promises must respect existing commitments.
requirements: Somalia is willing to receive American talks.
nodes.history: Political contact and a later strategic realignment are distinct.
nodes.rp: Early diplomatic contact is possible. Enhanced access and military aid need an actual rupture with the Soviet military relationship and defensive commitments.

nodes.title: Preserve Kagnew Access
nodes.description: Kagnew offers a communications and intelligence relationship. Washington can finance its continued use if the government controlling the site accepts the political bargain.
requirements: The communications facility is still usable.
Its actual territorial controller accepts American access.
nodes.history: Kagnew was a communications facility; continued use is an alternative.
nodes.rp: No radar tower or naval base is invented. Only one enhanced Horn funding priority is active at once. Losing access allows a later Somali realignment; both focuses remain completable.

nodes.title: Negotiate Berbera Access
nodes.description: Somali port access can support American operations in the western Indian Ocean. Mogadishu expects assistance, while Washington must limit the danger of inheriting its territorial conflict.
requirements: The Soviet military relationship has actually ended.
Somalia controls a usable Berbera port.
Somalia accepts a defensive aid and access protocol.
nodes.history: The access-for-assistance bargain followed the Soviet rupture.
nodes.rp: Docking rights do not grant unrestricted land military access. The bargain supplies no American war guarantee for an Ogaden offensive. It can replace a lost or ended Ethiopian priority.

nodes.title: An Ethiopian Training Mission
nodes.description: Training and sustainment can make existing American equipment useful without promising to satisfy every request for a larger army.
requirements: Ethiopia requests the mission.
The USA has 400 infantry weapons and 40 support equipment.
nodes.history: Training and limited assistance fit the existing relationship.
nodes.rp: This limited mission does not require Kagnew and does not prevent later diplomatic realignment. Deployment of American combat divisions remains a separate player decision.

nodes.title: A Somali Defensive Protocol
nodes.description: Defensive assistance can preserve the access bargain without endorsing a campaign to change Ethiopia's borders. Mogadishu must decide whether these limits are acceptable.
requirements: The accepted Berbera protocol is active.
Somalia is not conducting an offensive into the Ogaden.
The USA has 400 infantry weapons and 40 support equipment.
nodes.history: American deliberations drew a distinction between defence and Ogaden.
nodes.rp: An offensive into the Ogaden suspends this extra programme and new shipments. It does not erase delivered equipment or automatically declare war on Somalia.

nodes.title: Review the Horn Commitment
nodes.description: Facilities and partners can lose their value as circumstances change. An orderly review keeps access, assistance and military promises distinct.
effects: Unlock: End or Renew a Horn Programme
Unlock: Reassign the Enhanced Horn Appropriation
nodes.history: American commitments in the Horn changed over time.
nodes.rp: Both diplomatic channels stay open. A new enhanced programme replaces its competitor only after actual consent. Completed deliveries do not replay on renewal.

nodes.title: The Pretoria Channel
nodes.description: South Africa has influence over neighbouring conflicts, but cooperation with its government carries political costs across the continent. Contact is a means of negotiation, not an endorsement of apartheid.
requirements: South Africa receives American political talks.
nodes.history: Public pressure and private contact both featured in the 1976 diplomacy.
nodes.rp: No arms exemption or recognition of minority rule is implied. Applicable embargoes remain in force.

nodes.title: Quiet Leverage
nodes.description: Private pressure can seek a South African commitment to bring its regional partners into negotiations. Its usefulness depends on what Pretoria is actually prepared to concede.
requirements: South Africa accepts explicit pressure and reporting commitments.
nodes.history: A discreet bargaining approach has historical precedent.
nodes.rp: A stronger private channel competes for diplomatic funding with the enhanced Lusaka programme. Ordinary contact and public statements can still coexist. South Africa may refuse.

nodes.title: The Lusaka Declaration
nodes.description: A public commitment to majority rule can improve American credibility with African governments and liberation movements. It also narrows Washington's room to accommodate Salisbury.
requirements: An actual Rhodesian minority-rule dispute remains unresolved.
An African host accepts a public diplomatic initiative.
nodes.history: Kissinger publicly supported majority rule at Lusaka in 1976.
nodes.rp: An alternative enhanced funding priority, not a permanent ban on private diplomacy. Recognition and constitutional decisions stay with the countries concerned.

nodes.title: Support a British Conference
nodes.description: British sponsorship and African participation can give talks a political basis that unilateral American pressure cannot supply.
requirements: Britain agrees to sponsor the conference.
The Salisbury government and represented nationalist organisations accept participation.
nodes.history: British and African acceptance were essential to the conference effort.
nodes.rp: Refusal leads to another negotiating round. Neither the focus nor a US-Soviet understanding can sign for nationalist movements or replace a Rhodesian government.

nodes.title: Support the Agreed Transition
nodes.description: An agreed transition needs reconstruction and institutions capable of keeping the peace. American assistance should support the settlement the local parties actually made.
requirements: An inclusive transition has been accepted by the actual local parties.
The receiving government controls the reconstruction areas.
nodes.history: An earlier successful transition is a plausible alternative outcome.
nodes.rp: No instant independence, annexation, party swap or election result. The focus funds an already agreed transition and can continue under the legitimate successor government.

nodes.title: Deniable Pressure
nodes.description: Political contacts, financial assistance and selective pressure can challenge a hostile government before a friendly rebel state exists.
nodes.history: Existing US statecraft focus.
nodes.rp: The global political route complements the regional campaigns. A covert operation is not an offer that the targeted government must approve.

nodes.title: Political Operations
nodes.description: Organised local parties, media and political associations give American policy a foothold inside another country. Foreign support can amplify an opposition that still has to win domestic support.
nodes.history: Proposed extension of the existing US focus, using MD political mechanics.
nodes.rp: Political parties and protest pressure are separate. The purpose is to create a viable pro-Western alternative, then exploit a genuine political crisis. No independent rebel country is needed for these first steps.

nodes.title: Support Western Opposition
nodes.description: Use the existing political-manipulation action to strengthen the local Western party in the same political current as the American government. American influence and political capital are spent on the attempt.
requirements: The USA has a Western government.
The USA is among the target's three largest influencers with at least 30% influence.
At least 100 Political Power; the native 28-day manipulation cooldown has elapsed.
Native country-specific political protections permit the action.
effects: American influence in target: -10 percentage points
Supported party popularity: +1.2 percentage points at the native baseline
Western outlook popularity: +1.2 percentage points at the native baseline
nodes.history: Existing MD action. The displayed popularity example uses the unmodified native baseline.
nodes.rp: The native calculation changes with its actual inputs. The target party in the corresponding American governing-party slot retains its own local identity. This action does not change the government or require its approval.

nodes.title: Finance Protest Organisers
nodes.description: Fund political organisers during a confrontation with the target government. Pressure enters the existing national protest system, where domestic conditions and the government's response determine whether it lasts.
requirements: The USA has a Western government.
An existing local Western opposition has at least 10% outlook support.
The USA is a top-three influencer with at least 30% influence.
The target permits the native protest system and is outside its protest cooldown.
The target has not received this financing within 28 days.
No native protection against political intervention is active.
effects: United States Treasury: -0.0005% of current US GDP
nodes.history: New US decision proposal. It feeds MD protest strength and preserves the native warnings and countermeasures.
nodes.rp: The government cannot veto hostile opposition funding. It can counter influence, reform, fund police and suppress or appease native protests. Funding never resets its warning or revolt timers. Ordinary MD protest rebels are not automatically Western.

nodes.title: Back a Western Coup
nodes.description: Use the native influence-coup process to back the strongest represented Western party. Local support, government stability and competing influence shape the outcome.
requirements: The USA has a Western government.
The USA is the largest influencer in the target with at least 50% influence.
The target has a different outlook and is not an American subject.
More than 200 Political Power; the game rule permits Western coup actions.
Native country-specific political protections permit the action.
effects: United States Political Power: -200 on confirmation
nodes.history: Existing MD coup action, with the target's actual local party and native outcome weights.
nodes.rp: The native outcomes include a political takeover, a civil-war branch or failure and exposure. A high protest level alone does not guarantee a Western victory. No separate automatic regime-swap button is added.

nodes.title: Supply the Western Front
nodes.description: Once an actual armed partner exists, use the ordinary lend-lease channel to support it. A first shipment can be modest; further commitments remain separate American choices.
requirements: A real Western-aligned rebel government or partner force exists.
That recipient accepts the lend-lease offer.
The USA has the equipment it offers and an eligible delivery route.

assets: Illustrative agreed first shipment: infantry weapons -1,000
Illustrative agreed first shipment: infantry weapons +1,000

nodes.history: Existing military-assistance channel. The 1,000-weapon shipment is an illustrative offer, not an automatic reward.
nodes.rp: The real diplomatic offer sets quantities and delivery conditions. No virtual army or stockpile is created before a recipient exists. The USA chooses its own level of intervention.

horn: Somalia and the limits of American commitments, 1980

scope: US foreign-policy concept with current neighbouring entries and native global political actions. Not a full installed USA-tree layout.
rules: Basic channels can coexist. Enhanced funding priorities are exclusive only while active and can be reassigned after consent.
All monetary rates are percentages of current annual GDP; weekly rates are charged weekly without dividing by 52.
Political movement contacts precede statehood. Military assistance needs actual forces, stocks, routes and legal authority.
Governments approve their own cooperative commitments. A hostile government cannot veto opposition operations against it. Moscow cannot withdraw Cuban forces.
Standing bilateral programmes require participation, peace and bilateral sanctions clearance. Original temporary terms keep running during suspension; paid setup and equipment never replay.
Existing MD manipulation, coups and lend-lease are reused. Protest financing is the proposed extra US decision, not an already installed feature.
Effects are balance proposals. Native rendering, execution and live MP are not claimed.

reference_profile.md_donor: Main MD 05_russia.txt: SOV_acquire_drones and SOV_fly_byu_drones; native influence/protest systems
reference_profile.pattern: 35-day focus, country-scoped aid and mirrored real equipment removal/grant; native manipulation and coups remain their own authoritative actions.
reference_profile.icon_reference: Existing Generic and Russia goal medallions; private web typography approximates native labels.
